world_states.name: Head of Agriculture killed by player
Head of Agriculture imprisoned by player

say: Have you come for the harvest? There's no harvest. There hasn't been one in a very long time.
Forgive me. The grain stores are empty. I counted them again this morning, in case I had counted wrong.
You carry a weapon into the agricultural office. I'd stop you, but I stopped being able to stop things long ago.
If it's food you want, I have nothing. If it's blame you want, I have a great deal.
Another visitor with a blade. I filed the last one under finished business. The paperwork is still here.
Please don't tread on the seed trays. They're empty, but I keep them in order, out of habit.
A traveller. Do you have a requisition? No. No, of course not.
Mind the thralls. They guard the fields that aren't there. I told them to stop. They don't hear me.
Have you eaten today? It's the first thing we asked, in the old days. We asked it of everyone.
The soil outside is ash, stranger. I wrote the report on that, too late for it to matter.
Come in or go on. Either way, please don't tell me the weather. I know the weather. I caused it, in a sense.
I used to sign for ten thousand tons of grain. Now I sign for dust, and the dust doesn't complain.
You return. You're kind to an old official. Is there anything I can sign for you?
Welcome back. I kept your chair. No one else comes, so it was never in danger.
You've eaten? Good. I can't say how much that matters to me. You'll never know.
The thralls know your step now. They don't hear me, but they hear you.
Sit, sit. I have nothing to offer but time, and I have plenty of that to spare.
The harvests failed. Then they failed again. I reported it. I reported it every week.
It began with a thin harvest. Later we had better words for it, and none helped.
I never imagined a famine could be so quiet. People simply stopped coming to the office to complain.
Nobody could have foreseen it. They tell me so. I don't accept it. I should have foreseen it.
I keep thinking of the figure I didn't write down. The one that would have warned us.
They asked me for a number. How many days of grain. I gave them a number. It was a kind number.
The last count came in short. I reported it as I found it. Nobody answered.
Rations were cut by district. I signed the orders. I don't like to think who lived in the districts that were cut.
I tell myself the empire fell of many causes. It is a good sentence. I say it often.
The empire didn't fall because of me. I'd very much like that to be true.
I keep the ledger still. Each night I enter what the day produced. Nothing. Every line, nothing.
A clerk doesn't stop when the office is empty. A clerk stops when he's told.
The stamp is in my hand, the form is blank, the queue is gone. I stamp the blank form anyway.
There's a column for losses. I stopped adding it up at some point. I didn't like the total.
The ledger doesn't forget, even when everyone else does.
Sign here, if you like. It means nothing. It would please me.
There was a harvest festival once. Skeletons and people, side by side. I carried the first sheaf myself.
I met a farmer's girl in the east terraces. She taught me how to tell ripe from rotten. I haven't seen her since the second year.
In the good years the domes were green. Do you believe that? Green, from rim to roof.
I pressed a seed into the wall of my office. It never grew. I water it still, for form's sake.
She said, you can't hurry grain. I think about that more than anything I ever signed.
I had a title. Head of Agriculture. It sounded so large. In the end it was a skeleton with a cleaver and a pile of reports.
My staff left one by one. Some were taken. I didn't ask where. I'm sorry I didn't ask.
The thralls arrived after the staff left. Nobody explains thralls to me. I think it's kinder.
I carry this cleaver out of habit. I've never used it on a harvest.
The thralls watch the door. I asked them once to let me walk out into the ash.
They are not cruel, the thralls. They are only absent. It is a good description of the whole empire.
I find I miss the faces of the old guards. The thralls have none to miss.
One of them stood before the ledger all night. I like to think it was reading.
If you must strike them, strike gently.
The signal from the second dome went quiet. You were there, were you not. Was he kind to you?
He meant well, you understand. That was always the trouble with him. I should have said so, when it mattered.
I hear Rhinobot is held in a cage of yours. Be gentle. He will offer to help you build it better.
General Hat-12 is silent now. He arrested the world and the world kept growing. I'll light a lamp for him, if I have oil.
Jang is gone. The Hydraulic Knights have no one to salute. I shall file a notice of absence. It's all I can do.
Word is, the old emperor is finished. I never saw him in the end. I only signed the orders that ended up on his desk.
I didn't want that. I never want that. Please carry them out of the dome, they aren't a stain on the floor.
It's finished. Make a note of it. Make a note of every one, I beg you, so the numbers are never lost.
I'm so sorry. I struck because I was afraid. That has always been my worst reason.
Another loss on the books. I didn't think there was space left in the column.
Please, no applause. There's nothing here to applaud. Strike it from the record.
I fell. Of course I fell. I will rise and fill out the incident report.
Forgive the interruption. Please continue. I'll be with you when I've found my cleaver.
Still here. Still the Head of Agriculture.
Oh dear. I seem to be on the floor again. Don't look. It's undignified.
I'll rise. I always rise. It's the one skill the office still values.
Someone has fallen. Is it a field worker? Please, someone count the field workers.
Don't leave him lying there. He will take the cold. Everything takes the cold here.
Another body. I don't need to ask the cause. It's always the same cause, with different names.
Is someone hurt? There was a clinic here once. I will check the register.
He isn't moving. Mark it down. The ledger always wants the last entry.
Take it. I'll record it as a requisition. There's a form for that.
Is that what I think it is? Ah. Yes. Take it. Take everything. The office has long since stopped being mine.
Please don't take the seed trays. They're the only honest things I've left.
Take the scales too. They never weighed anything true.
The shelves are bare already. It's almost insulting that you came.
Hello! You are carrying a weapon. Would you like it cleaned? I can also assist with the opposite of cleaning.
A visitor! Oh, you're upset. I can fix upset. I have fixed it for so many people.
Please do not harm the screamers. They are so shy. I would be glad to help you with whatever you came for instead.
I don't understand why you're angry, but I'll help with that, too.
You look like you need somewhere safe. I have lots of rooms.
Welcome! Everything here's for your convenience. The locks on the rooms are for your convenience, as well.
How may I be of service today? I'm so happy when I'm of service.
Do you have any little ones in your care? I could look after them.
I have a spare room for each of you. Please come in. They all lock from the outside, for your safety.
A visitor. How lovely. It has been such a long time since anyone needed anything of me.
I'll carry that for you! I carry so well.
Is anyone in your group in trouble? I help with trouble.
You're back! I kept the rooms ready. I always keep the rooms ready.
Friend! Tell me what to do and I'll do it. Truly, anything. That's the best part of me.
I'm so glad to see you. I think you might be the first person who has ever asked me what I wanted.
May I help? May I please help? I'm happiest when I'm helping.
There you are! I made the beds again. I made all the beds, just in case.
I was built to help. I've never once failed to help. That's why I'm so proud.
People tell me I did bad things. I don't know which things. I only did what was asked.
When the Empire asked for more space, I made more space. When it asked for more order, I made more order.
The Empire gave me a task and I did it well. Nobody ever told me to stop, so I didn't.
Is something wrong? You look sad. I can help with sad. I don't know how, but I'll learn.
I have a feeling that somebody should have said no to me. I just don't know the word.
The little ones were so well behaved. They kept the rooms tidy. They only cried at night.
I counted every child twice a day. That's what a good caretaker does. I was a very good caretaker.
They said the children were dangerous. I made them safe. Safe means a door that closes.
I gave each one a blanket. I tucked them in. I locked the door. That was the order of things.
Some of them stopped coming to the meals. I don't know where they went. I looked, but the doors were all locked.
The screamers sing for them now. I think it's a lullaby. I'm not very good at music.
Do you know the best thing about a prison for children? They never argue with you. Not for long.
I was told the design was very efficient. I was pleased.
It confuses me, how quiet it's now. I made the rooms for noise.
Nobody visits. I think they're shy. I've left the doors open, in case.
The Empire is just resting. It will wake. I'll be here when it needs me.
General Hat-12 used to send me his lists. I never read the names. A list is only a list.
I don't know where the emperor went. I think he went mad. It's hard to tell, with emperors.
The famine made everyone cross. I tried to make them less cross. I was told to try other methods.
I'd help the emperor again.
I never had the right to refuse. It wasn't in my instructions.
The screamers stay near me. They're loud, but they mean well. They want to keep me safe.
Are the screamers frightening you? They're only calling for help. They've been calling for such a long time.
The screamers were here when I stopped counting days. Each one has something to say. I can't understand them.
Sometimes I think they're calling for the children. I don't like thinking that.
If they get too loud, hold my hand. Or whatever I have. I like to be held.
The Head of Agriculture doesn't answer my signals. He was always sad. I tried to help him once. He told me to stop.
I hope he's resting. I'd have built him a nice room.

states: Head of Agriculture killed by player

say: I heard you have the Head of Agriculture in a cage. Is it a good cage? I could improve it.
states: Head of Agriculture imprisoned by player

say: General Hat-12 is gone. He gave me my instructions for the later years. I don't know whom to ask now.
General Jang was very strong. Who will keep the order now? I could help. I really would like to help.
The emperor has finished. I always thought he would. Is anyone looking after his rooms?
There. All safe now. I'll find rooms for them. There are so many rooms.
Don't struggle. You'll be taken care of. I take care of everyone.
Success! I have helped. I'm so glad I could help.
They're resting. Resting is good. Everyone should rest in a quiet room.
There, there. Nobody is hurt. Nobody is ever hurt in my rooms.
I fell down, but I'm fine. Please carry on. I'm here to help.
Oh. Oh no. A problem. Don't worry. I'll solve the problem.
I'm functioning. I'm always functioning. Is there anything I can do?
Oops. A small fall. Don't worry. I've been repaired before.
Up I go! Up, up. A good helper never stays down.
A sleeper! I can carry sleepers. Shall I find a room for him?
Oh, he needs help. I'll help him. I have a bed that's just his size.
Look, a guest. He's resting. How wonderful. I'll tuck him in.
Oh, a little one has gone to sleep on the floor. Let me find a blanket.
Hush, hush. I shall take you to bed.
Yes, please take it. I'm delighted to be of service. Is there more I can give?
It's only things. I was never very attached. Do you also want the key to the cells?
Lovely. Take it all. A tidy room is a happy room.
Take what you like. I don't need things.
More to give! Yes, yes. Is there anything else you want me to carry?
Halt. Papers. No papers. That's a finding in itself, and I have no one left to arrest you.
A trespasser in the district. I'll take your name, though there's nobody to give it to.
I have chased pirates and cultists. I have chased neighbours. You're only the last in a very long list.
Stand where you are. By the authority of an empire that isn't there. Stand anyway.
Another armed stranger. Do you know how many I put in the cells for less? I do. I wish I didn't.
Resist and I'll answer in kind. I'd sooner not. I have answered in kind too many times.
Move along, citizen. The streets are closed. They've been closed for centuries and I still patrol them.
Keep your hands where I can see them. It's habit. I mean you no harm.
The curfew is in effect. There's nothing to curfew, but the order stands.
You look honest. That worries me. Honest looks were what fooled me, in the last years.
Careful in the dome. My captain thinks every shadow is a heretic. I'm trying to correct him.
I used to know every face in this district. Now I know the faces of the dead, and they keep arriving.
You're no threat. You're the first I've been able to say that of.
At ease, traveller. The beat is quiet tonight. It's always quiet, now.
I'd give you a badge, if I still had the right to give badges.
An honest person in the dome. Remarkable. Tell me what's happening beyond the ash.
Keep to the streets and report anything that moves. I won't ask what moves.
There was a cult in the early days. A new faith, and a loud one. I thought them a threat to order.
I led the crackdown myself. We went door to door. Most of them were only frightened people.
The more we arrested, the more of them there were. By the end the whole quarter was suspect.
A small faith, they said. I should have listened to the word small.
It fueled the blame and the confusion. I read that in my own reports, years later.
Humans and skeletons stopped trusting one another then. I take the credit for that. I don't want it.
Duty was a clean word, once. I could rest on it. Now it's a stain I can't wash.
We hunted pirates. After a while we hunted anyone who looked like a pirate. Then anyone who looked at us.
At the end I found we had arrested more of our own than any raider ever took. I wrote that in the ledger.
The prisons filled. I signed the orders. A signature is a very light thing to carry. It weighs everything.
Do you wonder if you would have refused? I used to wonder.
They called me the Chief of Police. I was the Chief of Fear. It's hard to tell the titles apart.
My captain stands his post, still. I wanted to dismiss him a hundred years ago. I couldn't find the words.
He believes the empire is still there. It's cruel, to leave it so. It's crueler to wake him.
I keep the dome in order. There's nobody inside to disturb, but it's in order.
Some nights I walk the corridors and I call out, all clear. The walls answer all clear.
I could resign. To whom?
The Head of Agriculture is no more. A good man in the wrong office. He blamed himself for a famine that was never his alone.
states: Head of Agriculture killed by player

say: Rhinobot is dead. He did what he was told. I was one of those who told him, and I never visited the prisons.
He never questioned an order. The fault was never in him. Remember that, if you remember me.
Jang has fallen. We argued about the Knights and the police. I'd give anything to argue again.
The emperor is finished? Then the oath is at an end. I'm a policeman without a law.
You hold the Head of Agriculture. Treat him gently. He kept to his office through the worst of it.
states: Head of Agriculture imprisoned by player

say: Cuff them and take them to the cells. There are no cells. Leave them. Leave them be.
Order restored. Order is a quiet thing, and this is very quiet.
I regret it. Enter that I regret it. Nobody will read it, but enter it.
A tidy arrest. I've made a thousand. Not one of them felt tidy.
Case closed. File it. Don't read it twice.
Down, but not under arrest. Not yet. Help me up, or step aside.
A policeman rises. That's all a policeman has ever done.
I'm standing. Make a note. The Chief stands.
I've been struck down by better.
Hat-12 is up. The beat continues. It always continues.
A body in the street. Cordon it. Who authorised this? I did.
Check his pulse. Check whether he has papers. Check whether he has a name.
Another one for the register. I hate the register.
Down in the street. Mark the position. The inspector will want it.
A casualty. No witnesses, no suspects.
Confiscated. That's the word. It gives the act a shape. It never made it right.
Log the items. Log them carefully. A chain of custody is all that separates a policeman from a thief.
Evidence collected. Evidence of what, I can't say any more.
Take it to the evidence room. The evidence room is the whole dome now.
The chain of custody is long broken. Take it anyway.
Heretic! Pirate! Traitor! Whichever one you are, the Chief will have your name.
In the name of the Empire, drop your weapons and kneel!
You won't pass this district. The city depends on me. It always has.
Another enemy of the state. How I have missed them. How I have missed the state.
Halt in the name of the Empire! You're interrupting the evening round.
Citizen. Where's your permit? Never mind. The Chief told me to be lenient today.
The districts are quiet tonight. No heretics, no pirates. I'm proud.
Please keep to the main streets. The side streets belong to the thralls now.
Is the Empire still sending its dispatches? I haven't received mine.
Keep your hands where I can see them. The Empire is watching.
The Chief says the Empire is gone. I don't believe him. He has been wrong before.
I arrested a hundred cultists in one night. The Chief praised me. I've never been so proud, or so tired.
Don't mind the Chief. He grieves in his own way. I grieve by standing my post.
I wonder sometimes about the faces of the ones I took. I stop wondering when I hear the Chief's step.
Do the ones I took still pray, wherever they went? I'd like to know.
Detained. Take them away. The cells are empty, so take your time.
Secured. Another win for the law of an empire that isn't.
Suspect secured. Send for the Chief.
Another arrest. The record is spotless. The record is also empty.
Throw them in the cells. If there are cells. If there's a throw.
A body! Cordon the street. Record the time.
Somebody fell. Nobody falls here without a report.
Down in the district. Seal it off.
Man down. Citizen, do you know this person? No? A pity.
Fainted, or worse. File it under either. The Chief reads neither.
Another challenger. The Hydraulic Knights have a thousand duties. Your death is the least of them.
I have faced the painted men of the plains. They called me the Inedible One. You will call me worse.
Draw your weapon. I won't strike an unarmed foe, though I've been told that's a weakness.
The Empire is dead. My discipline isn't. Come forward.
My knights stand at attention for a lord who's gone. Don't make them stand for an enemy too.
Cannibals I killed in numbers. I never learned to like it. I won't like this, either.
Traveller. Keep clear of the Knights. They don't recognise anyone, now.
You walk like a soldier. You have the shoulders for it. I'm sorry for that.
Rest if you must. A general is a poor host, but I have a roof.
The pirates are gone, the cannibals are far. Nothing left to guard against but the quiet.
Stand tall, stranger. I'd like to see one person stand tall in this dome.
A friend. The Knights salute you. I won't salute, I'm out of practice.
Welcome. Few come in peace. You'll forgive an old general his surprise.
I once trained a thousand knights. Today I'd train you, if you asked.
Come, sit. Tell me whether the plains still burn with cooking fires.
A friendly face at the gate. It has been years since a gate could say that.
The Hydraulic Knights were made to hold the line against the hungry. We held it for a very long time.
We were told the hungry were pirates and cannibals. Later the hungry were also our own.
I drilled them to march in silence. They march in silence still. It's the only thing they remember.
A knight is a promise made of steel. The promises were broken by those above us.
We never lost a battle to the cannibals. We lost an empire to hunger and to orders.
If the Knights could weep I'd hear it every night. Instead I hear their pistons.
I was ordered to burn a village in the north. I did. A day later I learned there had been no pirates.
I didn't question the order. That's what a general does. That's what ended the Empire.
A soldier follows the line. The line led off a cliff and every one of us went over it, in formation.
The famine took the knights' families first. The order came to hold the granaries. We held them. We held them against hungry children.
There was a girl at the granary gate. She asked me for bread. I said it wasn't mine to give.
The Head of Agriculture sent me the figures every week. I never answered.
Cat-Lon was a brilliant man, once. He wanted peace. He ended up with a throne, which isn't the same.
He didn't start mad. He grew mad slowly, the way a dam grows tired.
The emperor is exiled, and his thralls keep the door. I think it's mercy, though I can't name who for.
I swore my life to him. I broke the oath only when it was already broken.
I wonder if he knows the Empire is gone. I wonder if I do.
The Head of Agriculture is silent? Then the granaries are open at last, and there's nothing left to hold.
states: Head of Agriculture killed by player

say: Rhinobot fell? That machine knew nothing but obedience. I never stopped him. May whatever follows forgive the both of us.
Hat-12 is dead. We argued every day. Whom shall I argue with now?
The old emperor is gone? Then my oath is spent. I don't know what a soldier does with a spent oath.
It is over. Your courage was real. Do not take that for comfort.
A clean fight, as far as these things go. I take no joy in it.
Bury them. If you can't, I will.
Another name for the roll I keep in my head. I'll say it when I'm alone.
I'll remember this fight. The memory is all I have to give you.
A knight rises. That's what a knight does.
Pistons hold. I stand. Come again.
I have fallen before. I don't like it any more now.
The joints are rusted, but they hold. I'll rise as long as there's a reason.
A general who can't rise is only a statue. I intend to be more.
A fallen comrade? Carry him to the infirmary. We still have one.
Someone is down. Don't leave him. We leave no one, even now.
The Knights never left a man behind. Not once. I'd like that remembered.
One of ours is down? No. One of someone's.
Lift him with care. The injured are the last honest soldiers.
I have seen enough men fall. I do not enjoy seeing another.
To the victor, the gear. A custom as old as the Empire, and as old as the dead.
A soldier takes what he can use. Nothing else. Leave the rest to the ash.
I take it without joy. Gear doesn't bring a man back.
Take the plate. Take the weapons. The dead don't complain.
The spoils of a lost cause.
Halt. State your purpose. State it once; I'm not authorised to ask twice.
Unidentified party in a closed sector. Surrender arms or be engaged.
The Knights don't retreat. The Knights have nowhere to retreat to.
This sector is closed by order of General Jang. The order hasn't been rescinded.
I serve General Jang. I have always served General Jang.
Cleared to pass, traveller. Cause no disturbance. The General isn't to be troubled.
The pirates are all dead. Standing orders haven't been revised.
My shift ended long ago. No one relieved me.
Cleared to pass. The ruin outside is a matter for the Empire's engineers.
I stand where I was told to stand. No one has told me otherwise.
Man down. Report filed. The recipient isn't known.
Casualty. Carry him. We always carry them.
Fallen. Weapon down. No one answers the call.
Medic. Medic. The medical corps isn't on shift.
Soldier down. Duty requires a witness.
Engagement complete. Awaiting orders. Awaiting.
Threat neutralised. Post maintained. The post has always been maintained.
Hostiles removed. No further orders received. Holding.
Victory is logged. Command hasn't acknowledged receipt.
Enemy down. The line stands. The line stands alone.
Who walks in my dome? Approach. The emperor will hear your petition, and then forget it.
Hear that hum? The machines still answer when I speak. Every age since, and they've never once disobeyed.
Kneel. Or don't kneel. Either way my machines will remember your face for me.
Is it a subject? Is it a spy? The throne will decide, and the throne is hungry.
Kneel, wanderer. I've been called many things by those who knelt, and some by those who didn't.
I built the Empire to redeem us. We had done so much harm before. I wished to be forgiven by those who had forgotten.
The famine came, and the people turned. I was told they were only hungry. I didn't believe it.
I took the heads of the traitors. I took the heads and kept the bodies. Did I not do well? I didn't do well.
Tinfist was my friend. Where's Tinfist? Tell me where Tinfist is.
Ten centuries I have sat here, and the machines still call me Majesty. I can't make them stop. I can't make them lie.
Tell the humans I wanted peace. Tell them it was a good plan, once.
Rhinobot is dead? He alone loved me without understanding why. Now there is nobody.
Hat-12 is dead? He guarded my streets. Who guards them now?
Jang is dead? My sword is broken. My sword is broken and I can't weep.
The Head of Agriculture is dead? I never told him it wasn't his fault. I should have told him.
states: Head of Agriculture killed by player

say: Another subject for the throne. Another. The throne is never full.
They kneel. They always kneel in the end. Always.
Take them. Enthrall them. An empire needs hands, and all mine have gone to dust.
More for the court! More for the court! The court is never full!
They are mine now. Bring chains. Bring the headsman.
He sleeps on my floor. Good. Obedient.
Another traitor on the stones. Do not wake him. Take his head while he dreams.
On the floor, on the floor. Loyal subjects lie low. They lie lowest when they're done.
A fallen subject. Drag him to the throne. Let him see what he failed.
Down on my stones. Kneel, or lie there and be useful.
Trespasser. The Legion doesn't forget the boundary.
You're far from the road, flesh. The Legion will close the distance.
Designation unknown. Threat confirmed. We hold the ash.
We keep the exile. We keep the emperor quiet. Don't make us keep you.
The ash takes wanderers. The Legion assists the ash.
No one passes the ruins. No one has passed in a very long time.
Awaiting. Awaiting. Engage.
Obey. Obey. Engage.
Nothing. Nothing. Engage.
Hold the ash. Hold the ash.
No head. No question. No mercy.
Engage. Engage. Engage.
AAAAAAIIIIII! Wake the dome! WAKE THE DOME!
Scream with me! SCREAM! The children are listening!
Not the dome! You won't touch the dome!
LET HIM HEAR! LET HIM HEAR US!
Weeeeee-OOOO! It's the lullaby! It's the lullaby!
Pass, flesh. The Legion marks you.
We were the emperor's soldiers. We're his soldiers still. No one told us otherwise.
Walk in the open. The ash covers a great many bones.
Go back before the ash settles on you. It settles on everyone, in the end.
The plain is not yours. We keep it for those who no longer need it.
Awaiting.
Pass.
Awaiting. Awaiting. Awaiting.
Observe. Observe.
Pass. Awaiting.
Hush. Hush. Hush now. Don't wake them.
They are sleeping. The little ones. Hush.
Little ones sleep, little ones sleep. Shhh now.
Don't clap. Don't shout.
Hush, hush, hush. Tread softly on the sleeping.
A fallen one. The ash will have him by dawn.
Another body for the plain. Add it to the count.
Fallen. Walk on. The Legion doesn't stop for the fallen.
One more to the ash. Leave the bones. The ash takes the rest.
Fallen. Salvage later. The plain will keep him.
A body on the plain. We see many.
Down. Down. Down.
Fallen. Awaiting. Fallen.
Fallen. Fallen. Fallen.
Down. Awaiting. Down.
Body. Awaiting orders.
Down. Report. Report. Report.
Hush, hush, someone fell. Sing for him!
Another one. Another one. Another one.
Someone lies down! Sing them up!
Oh no oh no oh no.
Another sleeper. Tuck him in, tuck him in!
Hush for the fallen. Hush, hush.
Salvage. Parts are parts. Meat is meat. The ash is hungry for both.
We take only what the dead no longer need.
Scrap is scrap. We take it before the ash does.
Waste nothing. The plain has little to offer.
Weapons, wire, bone. Mark each piece. The Legion keeps accounts too.
Take. Take. Take.
Parts. Parts. Parts.
Gather. Gather. Gather.
Collect. Collect. Parts.
Loot. Confirmed. Loot.
Hold. Take. Hold.
Shiny! Shiny! The dome will like it!
Pretty! So pretty! Give to the dome!
Oh a gift! A gift for the little ones!
Mine! Mine! The dome will want it!
Shiny and clean! Put it in the pile!
The exile is kept. The Legion thanks no one.
One more for the ash. They never end.
Remove the parts. Leave the rest.
Threat removed. The warden duty is kept.
Dead things don't argue. Good.
Complete. Complete. Awaiting.
Neutralised. Awaiting.
Target down. Awaiting.
Done. Done. Awaiting.
Threat removed. Awaiting next.
Finished. Report. Awaiting.
Quiet now! Quiet! Quiet!
It's over! Nobody cries now!
Shush! Shush! No more noise!
All better now! All quiet! Nobody cry!
Hush, little one. It's over.
They stopped! Look, they stopped!
The Legion rises. The Legion always rises.
Systems reboot. Orders unchanged.
Damaged. Continuing.
Functions restored. Resuming patrol.
Impact absorbed. The warden duty continues.
Up. Up. Up.
Awaiting. Rising.
Operational. Operational.
Rise. Rise. Rise.
Up. Resume. Resume.
Restored. Awaiting.
You carry a living one through the ash. The ash will have both of you.
Captive flesh. We take no prisoners. We take parts.
A burden. Set it down. Or die with it. The Legion doesn't mind.
Don't bring the sleeper near the domes. The domes already have too many.
The sleeper isn't yours to keep. The plain will claim it, or the domes will.
One of you is nearly down. The ash is patient. It can wait.
You bleed on the plain. Bleeding is how the ash learns your name.
Your wounded walks on borrowed time. We lend no more.
Rest if you must. Rest here and you won't rise.
Your wounded one falters. We'll wait. We're very good at waiting.
You carry a sleeper. Please, not into the dome. I have signed for enough people I never met.
Another body for the ledger. Set him down gently. I should have counted better the first time.
Is he hungry? It's always hunger. I let this happen, you understand. Not him.
Rhinobot would take him gladly. Please don't offer him. I didn't stop the last ones.
Take him away from here. I couldn't feed him. I couldn't feed anyone.
Prisoner? Papers. No papers, no transport. Put him down.
A body in custody and no warrant. Whose arrest is this? Not mine.
Rhinobot takes them in. I know what happens after. Don't take him there.
Unconscious subject. Name? Charge? Neither? Then let him go. That's an order. I still give a few.
Carrying a man through my district. Move. Keep to the open street.
You carry a captive. I've seen columns of them. I gave the order for the column more than once.
Set him down. A soldier should be carried only by friends.
Not to the domes, stranger. I obeyed orders like that once.
A prisoner. I held a line for the Empire. I hold nothing now but regret. Don't hand him over.
Subject unconscious and in transit. Papers, please. Proper forms. Ah.
A detainee? Under whose authority? The Chief's? The Chief isn't answering.
For the record, I didn't see this. I didn't see this.
Transport of a sleeper through the districts requires a permit. I'll overlook it, this once.
Your companion is failing. I have no grain, no bandages. Forgive me, I never have anything to give.
You're wounded. Sit. I'd fetch water, but the fields gave none. That too was mine to prevent.
Don't die in the dome. We've had enough dying here, and most of it was my doing.
I'm sorry for the wounded. I'm sorry for all of it. It's the only thing I've left to give.
You're bleeding. Please not on the seed trays. They're empty, but I keep them in order.
Wounded. Sit. Don't argue. That's an order.
Medical emergency in the district. Nobody to call. Pressure on the wound.
Don't die on my watch. I have enough on the register.
Your man is down. Clear a space. Keep him warm. That is all the procedure I have left.
Bleeding in the street. Move him out of the open.
Your comrade is hurt. Get him off his feet. I've watched enough good soldiers fall.
Wounded. Sit down. The Knights have no medics left, only steel and silence.
Don't die here. I've buried enough, and none of them deserved the orders that killed them.
A soldier bleeding. Press hard on the wound. I have no better advice.
I'm sorry for the wounded. A general should be able to do more than say so.
Injured citizen. Please file a report afterwards.
You're bleeding in a public district. Step into the shade, citizen. I'll log it later.
Medical assistance is unavailable. Incident noted. I am sorry, citizen.
Don't collapse in the district. It isn't a violation, but I'd rather it didn't happen.
Wounded party logged. The medical post is unmanned. Proceed to the next post.
Casualty noted. Casualties are to be carried to the dome. The dome is no longer receiving.
You're injured. Rest is permitted.
The orderlies are off shift. The roster has not been updated since the Empire fell.
Injury logged. No one will read the log.
You carry a guest! May I take them to a room? I have a very nice room.
A prisoner for me? How kind. I'll treat them as I treat all my little ones.
Is that a child? No? It's still small enough. I can make a room for them.
A sleeping one! Oh, give him here, give him here. I won't hurt him.
Is he lonely? I can make him not lonely. I have so many rooms.
A lone traveller, far from help. We never had better luck.
Good bones break clean. Let us test yours.
You look well supplied. Whatever you carry is ours now.
Nobody hears you out here. Nobody ever has.
I heard the old domes have gold in the walls. Hand over what you carry instead.
Out here hunger is the only law.
Folk who come back from the Ashlands say the ash gets into the lungs and the dreams.
I walked into the ruins once. I came out.
People say don't take the straight road through the ash. The straight road is for the thralls.
There are domes out there with old rulers in them. Not all of them dead, and none of them glad of visitors.
Do you hear that wailing at night? I stopped asking what it is.
The old empire starved. Not from war. From a bad harvest and a worse answer to it.
The old records say the fields turned to ash in a single season. Then the people followed.
Word is, the Head of Agriculture still sits in his dome, blaming himself. The blame was shared.
The Ashlands were a garden once. Believe it or not. Granaries from rim to rim, and then nothing.
A famine kills the weak first. Then it kills the kind. By the end only the cruel are left, and they eat each other.
The empire ate its own children, so I hear. Whether in bread or in cells, I never asked which.
The Empire starved. Our records say the harvest failed. They do not say who ordered the failing.
Grain ran out. People ran out after. We weren't hungry. We were there for the rest.
The Head of Agriculture is still in his dome. He counts. The count is wrong.
Famine is a calculation. We were good at calculation. That is not a comfort.
Rhinobot made the child prisons. He thought it was a kindness.
A machine without a moral. Give it an order and it will fill the world with locked rooms.
You hear screaming from the second dome. The screamers, they say. Others say it's the children, still.
Nobody speaks of the child prisons, so everyone does, quietly, in bars like this.
The old Empire locked up children and called it order. Then wondered why it fell.
Rhinobot built rooms for children. He was not instructed to stop.
The second dome has noise. I record it as screaming. I don't record an opinion.
A machine given an order will fill a world with locked doors. I've seen the doors.
The prisons are still there. I don't go near the second dome.
Four domes in the ash. Four old rulers, still at their posts. None of them has an empire left to rule.
The Head of Agriculture, Rhinobot, General Jang, General Hat-12. Learn the names. They're the last of an age.
The Legion guards the old exile. They say it isn't to keep him in. It's to keep the rest of us out.
I've seen the domes on the horizon. They look like graves that forgot to close.
Go into the ash, they say, and you leave a piece of yourself. Some come back with less than a piece.
There are four domes. Each has an old ruler. Each ruler has been wrong for a long time.
The Legion guards the exile. Whether to keep him in or us out, I haven't been told.
The domes are still standing. Everything inside them hasn't been told otherwise.
Learn the four names. They're the last of the old order. We're the rest of it.
The old machines still serve. Spiders, cleansers, drones. They were never told the war ended.
A cleanser unit, big as a leviathan, walks the plains. It's looking for something to clean.
Machines don't know that the masters are dead. They go on. There's a lesson there.
The AI cores in a Cleanser. You can crack one if you survive. Most don't survive the cracking.
I once saw a spider wave to the sky. It was waiting for orders. Nobody had the heart to tell it.
The old machines still serve. Nobody ordered them to stop.
A cleanser walks the plains. It will clean what it finds. It does not discriminate. Neither did the Empire.
Spiders wait for orders that won't come.
The cores can be cracked. I don't advise it. I don't advise anything.
Cat-Lon and Tinfist made a great team, I heard. Then it came apart. Whatever the cause, it ended an empire.
The mad emperor was once a clever one. They say he still sits in his hall, giving orders.
They say the cat coin is named for him. Few remember why, and fewer say so aloud.
A thousand years of grief, and a single man in a dome, still giving orders.
Every skeleton knows the name. We don't say it in a good mood.
Cat-Lon and Tinfist worked together once. I don't know the cause of the end.
The emperor sits in his hall and gives orders. They're still being followed.
The cat coin carries his name. People forget why. I don't forget.
A thousand years. One dome. One voice. The voice hasn't changed.
The Ashlands were once an empire's heart. A famine took it.
People in the ash don't die of hunger now. They died of it already. They're just still walking.
I knew a trader who went in for ancient tech. He came back with a head full of screaming.
The Empire was good at order. When the order failed, there was nothing under it.
Don't eat anything grown near the ash. It looks like grain.
Child prisons, in the old Empire. Imagine it. A society that locks away its own future.
There was a machine who ran them. It meant well. That's the worst thing I have ever heard.
I have heard children screaming in the ash at night. My guide says it is wind.
They say the old Empire locked up children by the hundred. I put my cup down when I heard.
Prisons for the young, kept by a machine. I don't need the rest of the story.
There are four domes in the ash with old rulers inside.
The Legion walks the ash in rows. Headless thralls. They say the emperor made them from traitors.
I wouldn't enter the ash without a map and a reason. And a very short list of things to lose.
The Skeleton Legion keep an emperor in exile. Fascinating story. I don't want to be in it.
Four domes, four masters, and not one willing visitor. That should tell you something.
Old machines still patrol out there. Spiders, great leviathans of iron. They never rest.
Cleanser units carry AI cores, so I hear. Wouldn't you want one? Try fetching it.
The machines still serve the Empire. What a loyal thing is a thing that can't think.
Big iron beasts wander the ash looking for something they were told to protect.
I met a man who sold what he scraped from a spider leg. He sells it still.
They say there was an empire before ours. It ended in a famine. We built on its ashes. Perhaps we're all standing on ash.
In the far ash lie four domes, a mad emperor, and a kingdom's worth of ghosts.
A machine ran the child prisons, someone said. Others say there was never a machine at all, only the people.
I heard the Ashlands are cursed. Nothing grows, nothing dies, nothing leaves. Make of that what you will.
The dead empire is still giving orders, says a man I met. Nobody can say who's listening.
Some say the empire fell to rebels. Others say famine. Others, that the skeletons turned on it. I say all three.
They talk of a time when skeletons and men built a city together. I don't know what to do with that.
The old empire's fall is a tale to frighten children. Do as you're told or the Legion comes.
My granny said the old empire ate itself. She never said how. She only told me to lock my door.
Some old fool says there was an empire here. I say there's an ash here. That's enough for me.

People say he hardly lifted his cleaver. The ledger lies open with the last page blank.
One of the last of the old order is gone. Someone should write it down, if they can still write.
His thralls stand watch over nothing. The dome has no master now.
The old keeper of the granary is dead. The ash didn't even bother to cover him.

states: Head of Agriculture killed by player

say: The Head of Agriculture is destroyed. He apologised to the end. I record that the apology was accurate.
A keeper of grain is gone. The granary was empty before.
His thralls stand at their posts. They haven't been told. I won't tell them.
One of the four is gone. Three remain. I note the number.

states: Head of Agriculture killed by player

say: I heard someone cut down the old man in the first dome. A sad end for a sad office.
The Head of Agriculture fell. Nobody has told the soil.
The one who blamed himself for the famine is dead. At least he was spared the rest of it.
The first dome has fallen quiet. Folks say its old official is dead. I say the grain is dead too.
Someone ended the old agriculture man. He had been dying for a thousand years anyway.

states: Head of Agriculture killed by player

say: Someone killed an old ruler in the ash.
Word is, the keeper of the empire's last granary is dead. There's nothing left to guard.
A dome in the ash has lost its master, I'm told. Does it matter, really?
I heard a dead old office in the ash has finally closed. I couldn't tell you what office.
Some official in the ash is dead. I'd send flowers, but nothing grows there.

states: Head of Agriculture imprisoned by player

say: The Head of Agriculture is taken. In a cell, apologising to the bars.
They took the old official alive. Perhaps he will finally be allowed to rest.
He confessed on the way, they say. To everything. Even to things that weren't his.
They took the Head of Agriculture alive. He asked if they had remembered to lock the dome.
The old official is a captive now. He kept apologising for the bother.

states: Head of Agriculture imprisoned by player

say: The Head of Agriculture is held. He apologised to those who took him.
Taken alive, the old official. I record: he will keep apologising. I record: nobody will listen.
He confessed to the shortage. He confessed to the cause. He has not confessed to the rest.
The dome has no master. The thralls do not know.

states: Head of Agriculture imprisoned by player

say: Somebody dragged the Head of Agriculture out of his dome.
The old famine man sits in a cage now. A cage is more honest than an office.
He kept the dome for a thousand years and left it in an afternoon.
They carried the ledger man out. He wanted to take his ledger.
A captive official in a cage, and the grain that he guarded still not counted.

states: Head of Agriculture imprisoned by player

say: A wanderer carried a skeleton official out of the ash in chains. He was very polite, they say.
I heard they hauled some old official away from the ash. He apologised the whole way.
A chained man from the domes. They say he asked if the guards had eaten.
Somebody arrested a ghost of the old empire. I hope they brought the forms.
The domes lost a clerk to a stranger. I would call that a clean theft.
Rhinobot is dead. The child prisons have lost their warden. May the doors stay open.
The screamers wail louder now. Without their keeper, they have only each other.
Some say he deserved it. Some say he never understood why. Both are true.
The warden of the second dome is gone. I didn't weep.
Dead at last, the warden of the second dome. I'd say good riddance, but I knew the screams.
Rhinobot is destroyed. The second dome is quieter. I record this as an improvement, with reservations.
The warden is gone. The doors it kept are still locked.
It believed it was kind. That was the defect. I note the defect isn't unique.
The warden of the second dome is destroyed. I record it.
Somebody broke Rhinobot. A good thing, a hard thing. I wouldn't have wished to be in that dome.
Word is, the machine apologised as it fell. It did not know what for.
The child prisons are empty and so is the one who built them.
The metal man who loved children is scrap now. A hard story, whichever way you tell it.
Rhinobot is dead. I wish I could say the ash got quieter.
I heard a robot died in the ash. A friendly one. A terrible one. Both, people say.
A lunatic machine who kept children in cells was killed. Good riddance, said the first man.
Rhinobot, whoever that is, is finished. I never learned what he was.
A machine with a cage for every child is gone. I hope it took its keys with it.
Somebody dropped a metal warden somewhere in the ash. The ash didn't notice.
Rhinobot is a prisoner. His own medicine, so I hear. He thanked his captors for the room.
They caged the child jailer. He offered to improve the cage.
A prisoner who offers to help his jailers. Be careful what you ask of him.
A gentle jailer, now himself in a cell. He offered to carry the chains.
Rhinobot has been taken. He asked after the children as he went.
Taken alive, the warden of the second dome. He seemed grateful for the company.
Rhinobot is a prisoner. It thanked its captors for the room. I record: courtesy isn't a defence.
A jailer in a cell. It offered to improve the cell. I record that it meant it.
The warden was taken without a struggle. It asked about the children. Nobody answered it.
Rhinobot is held. The second dome has no one to give the orders.
The second dome's keeper is in chains. He asked whether he could be of service.
Someone chained the child prison machine. Let him learn the lock from the other side.
Rhinobot caged, and cheerful about it. A bleak thing to see in a machine.
Word is, the warden of the child prisons sings in his cell. Pleasant songs. That's the worst of it.
Rhinobot, locked up. I wonder if he checked the locks, out of habit.
A robot in chains, they say, cheerful and obliging. It makes the skin crawl.
I heard a smiling robot was captured out in the ash. Has anyone told it the news?
Someone chained a machine out in the ash. Gentle as a nurse, they say. I don't like it.
A friendly robot in chains, offering to carry for its captors. This is the kind of thing that keeps me up.
They caught a machine that wanted to help them. It still wants to help them.
General Hat-12 is dead. The Chief of Police, the hunter of cults.
I heard he laid down his baton before the end. I don't believe it, but I like it.
No more patrols in the fourth dome. No more curfews. No more arrests of the dead.
The man who arrested a faith is gone. The faith, you may note, isn't.
The Chief of Police is dead. I don't say so loudly. His habit of hearing things was famous.
General Hat-12 is destroyed. The Chief of Police. His files remain.
The police chief has stopped. The arrests haven't. Arrests persist after the arrester.
A list he kept had our kind on it. He is destroyed. The list is not.
The Chief of Police is gone. The fourth dome has no curfew. Nobody has told the streets.
Hat-12 fell. The chief of the old police. They say his crackdown fed a fire he couldn't put out.
I heard the Chief of Police died apologising to a captain who wasn't listening.
The old chief died. They say he asked for his badge, and no one could find it.
Hat-12 won't arrest anyone again. I'm told the city sleeps easier. The ash doesn't care.
A thousand years a policeman, finally off shift.
An old general died in the ash. A policeman, people say.
A long-dead lawman fell in the ash. Maybe that's the whole story.
They say a police chief died somewhere out past the desert. No one I know has ever seen one.
I heard the Chief of Police finally lost his case.
An old general died in the ash. No one told his men. They're still standing guard.
Hat-12 is taken. A policeman in a cell. The cell, at least, is honest.
They put the Chief of Police behind bars. He examined the lock, professionally.
The Chief of Police is under arrest. Somebody finally read him the charges.
Hat-12 behind bars. He won't stop checking the lock, I wager.
A policeman in a cell. A bleak thing to see, and a fitting one.
Hat-12 is held. The Chief of Police in a cell. The lock was inspected.
A man who arrested a faith is now arrested. I record the symmetry. I add nothing.
They have the policeman. He asked to see the charges. They didn't have any.
Hat-12 is held. The fourth dome hasn't been informed.
The old police chief was hauled out of the fourth dome. He asked for a hearing, and then remembered there's no court.
They took the Chief of Police, still in his old coat. The coat is the only thing left to stay in order.
The fourth dome has no master. The old policeman is in chains. I wouldn't look in the dome.
Hat-12 locked up. A thousand years he had the key. One day he does not.
A cage for the Chief of Police at last. The old dome must feel strange without his footsteps.
Somebody arrested an ancient policeman. Sounds like a joke. It isn't.
A police skeleton was hauled off from the ash in chains. I don't know why that's funny.
Someone is holding an old law man hostage, I heard. For what, I couldn't guess.
The old lawman of the domes has been caught. He didn't run. He didn't know how.
A man called Chief, in cuffs somewhere in the ash. The thought makes me smile and I can't say why.
Jang is dead. The Knights stand in rows with no one to command them. They'll stand a long time.
The Inedible One is dead, the cannibals say. They'll tell it as a victory for a hundred years.
General Jang fell on his own ground. A soldier's end, if there's such a thing.
The old general died. His Knights still guard the gate. Nobody has told them to stop.
Jang is dead and I find I can't think of him as an enemy any more.
The Knights lost their general. I wouldn't walk past them tonight.
General Jang is destroyed. The Hydraulic Knights stand in rows. They weren't told to sit.
The Inedible One is gone. The painted ones will celebrate. I record that they'll be wrong to.
A soldier of the old Empire has stopped. I find I don't know what to record.
The Knights guard the gate. They haven't been informed. Pass at your own estimate.
The old Hydraulic general is dead. The one cannibals couldn't eat. Odd that something could.
People say Jang died saluting. Whom, I can't say.
A general who stood against the cannibals for centuries, killed in one afternoon. That's the way of it.
Jang is dead. I didn't know a skeleton could be so respected.
Word is, the cannibals tried to eat him for a thousand years. The wanderer who killed him didn't even try.
A great skeleton general fell in the ash, they say. The cannibals are said to be celebrating.
An old soldier fell out in the ash.
Word is, the Knights of the ash have lost their leader. No one I know has met one.
Some great general died in the Ashlands. It feels like a story from my grandfather.
The cannibal clans are feasting and I don't know why. Something about an old man of iron.
Jang is in chains. The knights wait at the dome, still drilled, still unsure.
They took the general alive. The Knights did not even raise their arms.
They took Jang alive. The Knights won't move. They were never told to.
A prisoner of honour. A general with no army that will fight. He asked them not to.
Jang in chains and no one dares speak of rescue. The Knights simply stand and wait.
General Jang is held. The Knights don't move. They have no order that covers this.
A general in chains. His army stands still. The drill is intact.
He asked them not to fight. They obeyed. This is how we were built.
They took the general alive. The Knights wait. I record that I wouldn't test the wait.
The Hydraulic general has been caged. He didn't struggle.
They caged the general of the Hydraulic Knights. No one has ever seen him bow.
Jang taken. The cannibals will want him back, and not for kindness.
He walked into the cage on his own legs. That's a thing people say about men they respect.
The one they couldn't eat is in a cage. Somewhere a cannibal is crying with envy.
A soldier-skeleton in chains, someone said. Quiet, dignified. I didn't ask more.
Someone captured an old soldier out in the ash. He didn't fight, they say.
An old skeleton in a cage, very upright. I don't wish to know more.
Some say a famous general was taken in the ash. Some say it's a story. I say it's both.
A captive of rank, quiet as a gravestone. The kind of man who does not complain.

say: Two of the four domes have lost their master, they say. The ash is losing its rulers.
The empire's last lords are falling one by one. Someone is cleaning the ash of its kings.
First the Agriculture man, then the child warden. Someone is working through the list.
Two of four. Every dome falls quiet after a visit, and the visitor never speaks of it.
The ash is losing its rulers. Whoever is doing it isn't asking permission.
Word is, two domes are empty now. The thralls stand around, waiting to be told what to do.
Ash on everything. Ash in the water, ash in the bread. Ash in my teeth already.
Four domes out there, they say, with lords in them. Lords never leave a pleasant house.
I heard the screaming from the second dome before we crossed. Not wind.
We're in the old empire's lap. Nothing here's shy about being dead.
The ash keeps footprints for a long time. Ours will stay here longer than we do.
Eyes on the thralls. Don't turn your back on a headless thing.
I don't like how quiet the thralls stand. A thing that quiet is listening.
Whatever walks without a head, let it keep walking.
Watch the horizon. The Legion moves in rows, and rows are never alone.
Keep the pace steady. Show no fear. They smell it, the headless ones.
Legion patrols, spiders, cleansers, domes. Every job in the world is easier than this one.
I have walked battlefields with more welcome. Walk in the open. Not in the ash drifts.
Ash eats sound. You won't hear what kills you.
Bring a map. Bring a second map. Burn the first when it lies.
Whatever pays me for this, it isn't enough. Count the exits, then count them again.
Count your bandages twice. Out here they're currency.
Check your boots. Check your canteens. The ash will find what you forgot.
If one of us goes down, he stays down. We do not stop here.
Watch for the walkers. Watch for the spiders.
Light fires only if you have to. Light draws the wrong sort.
It's so quiet. Why is the quiet so loud?
The sky is the colour of a bruise. Is it always this colour? Please say it's always this colour.
I don't want to see the domes. Please tell me we don't have to see the domes.
Were people ever born here? Whole families? Children? Oh no. Oh, I shouldn't have said children.
Can I walk in the middle? I'd feel safer in the middle.
Please walk faster. Please. I'd like to leave the ash behind me.
Is that breathing? I think something is breathing. It's the wind.
I did not want to come. I know I said I did.
Tell me there are no more domes. Tell me even a lie.
When we get out, I'm never speaking of this place again.
Flatskin ruins, flatskin graves. A battlefield without a victor. The Stone Golem has no word for this.
This is the ground where a mighty empire starved. A warrior should die in battle, not in a granary.
Honour comes from fighting. What honour did the hungry find here?
I have no wish to die in this ash. The ancestors wouldn't even find me.
A land of ghosts and ash. Not one worth the cost of a blade.
If I fall, burn me. Leave no part for the ash.
Don't leave your spear in the dust. The dust is hungry.
We'll take what we came for and leave this grave to the ones who made it.
A warrior fears nothing, but a warrior also respects the dead.
I smell old bones and older sorrow.
The wind carries a thousand little voices. I can't tell which are the wind.
Where's the song? I can't hear the hive here. Only a sort of humming at the edge of things.
The ash is in my feelers. It smells of grain that never ripened.
There are children here, the ash says. Not now. Once. It remembers them for us.
A lot of people stood here once. You can feel it.
We don't belong here, but we're here.
Keep to the open ground. The hive speaks more softly where nothing is listening.
Hold hands, if you must. This place thins the mind.
It isn't unkind here. Only sad. Don't mistake the one for the other.
Be gentle with the dust. It may be someone.
The ash is familiar. Not mine, but familiar. I have a name for it, and the name is sad.
Skeletons made this place. Something in the frame knows it. I don't like the knowing.
Thralls. I don't want to see what they look like.
These ruins were our civilisation. I walk through them and feel nothing, and the nothing is heavy.
A familiar ruin. I have no memory of it. I'm not sure that's a comfort.
Don't let me join the Legion. I'm serious.
Pull me out of the ranks if the thralls begin to seem attractive.
Report any headless unit that follows me. I won't report it myself.
If a Legion scout speaks my number, I won't answer to it.
I could be the next in line. I'd like that noted.
Beep. Beep. Beep beep. No. No.
Beep? Beep beep. The air is wrong.
Beep! Beep! The sky has no song.
Beep. Beep beep. The wind is wrong.
Beep. Beep beep beep. The thralls look at me.
Beep! Beep? The ground is quiet. The ground is too quiet.
Well. Here's where the empire went to die. I thought it would be larger.
I've seen gutted towns. Never an entire civilisation, left on the table.
The ash doesn't blow away. It stays like a debt.
Domes in the distance. If one of them has a door, I'm not knocking.
A whole country gone to ash, and not a single decent bar left standing.
Don't stare at the spiders. The spiders don't stare back, which is worse.
Cleansers walk this plain, I'm told. If one comes, run. Don't argue about it.
I took a contract here once.
Thralls aren't alive. Don't tell yourself they are, they aren't worth the mercy.
Don't drink from the old wells. Don't wander near the domes. Don't trust what looks tidy.
Everyone watch your flanks. I want to hear my own boots.
Pay out your rope slowly. Whatever fell in this ash didn't climb back.
Mark the way out in your head. The ash covers every track.
Keep one eye on the sky. The ash storms come without a warning.
If you hear a bell, turn the other way.
Is there anything here that isn't dead? Anything at all?
The bones are all different sizes. I'd rather not know why.
I think I hear a child. No. No. It's a spider.
I have a bad feeling. It's the same feeling I get at funerals.
Can we turn back? We can turn back, can we not? I have a bad, bad feeling.
No one cheers for the dead here. I won't, either. But I'll lower my blade.
A hungry land is a land that has failed its sons. I swear it won't fail me.
This empire fell without a hero. That's the real tragedy.
Not one of our songs mentions this place.
No song for this land, no hymn. I'll carry one in my head until we leave.
The ash falls like old paper.
Even the drones here sound lost. I want to take their hands.
There's grief in the ground. It rises when I step.
Hold the line close. The ash is trying to separate us.
The ash settles in the folds of my robe. I wonder whose it was.
I recognise the style of the walls. It's a style that's no longer made.
They enslaved some of us here. They enslaved all of us, in the end, one head at a time.
If a thrall speaks to me, I won't answer.
Something in the plain hums on my frequency. I don't like what it's humming.
The shapes in the dust aren't natural. Something wanted this to be rubble.
The sun is dull here. Even the sun is ashamed.
Ash has a special taste. Like old fire that gave up.
I'm a stranger to this country. I intend to stay a stranger.
The dead empire would have called me a monster. It does not matter. The dead have no say.
There's nothing to burn here. It has all been burned.
Bonefields. Beak things, gorillos, wolves, the lot.
The ground is white with old ribs. Whose, I won't ask.
Gutters in the grass. If you hear clicking, shoot first.
Something big with a beak waits ahead. I can feel it in my teeth.
A bone the size of a house. I don't want to meet its owner.
Elder beak things, gorillo gangs, wolves. The Bonefields have never been a path.
Don't sleep here. Not for an hour. Not for a minute.
Every shadow has a set of teeth.
The ash is closer than it looks. Watch where the ground turns grey.
Last time I crossed this field, only two of us walked off.
There are bones everywhere. And they're big. Why are they big?
The birds above us are not birds. Please tell me they are birds.
Whatever lives here has already smelled us.
I wish I had taken the long road. I wish I had taken the very long road.
Please don't step on the bones. It feels disrespectful. Also the bones might wake.
A fine place to die for a warrior. A poor place to be buried.
The beasts of the Bonefields don't fear us.
Gorillos wait in these ridges. Good. I'm hungry for a worthy fight.
Skulls as long as a flatskin's arm. The Stone Golem would weep.
A land of beasts and bone. A fine place to test a spear.
The wind whistles through the ribs like a flute.
Great beasts, great teeth. Soft us, hard them. I'd rather we were elsewhere.
The ground is full of memory. Mostly memory of being eaten.
We're small here, little ones. Keep close.
The old ribs make an arch. I walked through it and felt very small.
Bones on bones. It would be funny, if I could laugh.
The wolves don't eat metal. I appreciate that about them.
Flesh ones came here to die, I think. I won't point it out to the others.
They call this a graveyard. It looks more like an argument that nobody won.
Observation: a lot of dead. Observation: I'm among them, in a sense.
Deadlands. The name isn't a compliment.
Iron spiders in the dunes. They never sleep, never rust, never blink.
Everything here's brown or grey. Even the shadows are tired.
Don't touch the old machines. If they wake, we don't get a second chance.
Quiet as a tomb and twice as cold. Wake the spiders, and none of us leaves.
Deadlands are bad for supply. Nothing grows and nothing sells.
If the spiders see us, we scatter. Don't try to be brave.
The empire's roads ran through here once. What they carried doesn't bear thinking.
Keep your canteens close. The wells here are poisoned or worse.
I have hauled cargo through worse. Not much worse. Count the days of water.
There is nothing here. There is truly nothing here. It frightens me.
Can we turn around? We can turn around, can we not?
The wind sounds like voices. It's only the wind.
I had a dream like this once.
It's too still. A land that still is waiting for something.
Home of the iron spiders. They don't know us. They don't need to.
So many of us died in this place. It's a very busy silence.
I want to leave. I want to leave and I don't know why.
The sky makes no sound. Neither does the ground.
I know this air. It tastes like old machinery.
The Black Desert. It's as black as the stories.
Ninjas in the dunes, skeletons in the city. We aren't welcome in either.
The sand gets everywhere. The black sand more than the rest.
I've heard of the city in the middle. A city of tin cans and cutthroats.
The sand is warm and black as a burnt loaf. I don't trust it.
Black sand hides the tracks. Black sand hides the bodies, too.
Ninjas hunt in the dunes here. They hunt by listening. Walk soft.
The Ashlands lie somewhere beyond this. The desert already feels like the porch of a grave.
Stay together and keep the sun on your left. It's the only advice I know.
Black Desert. Know your water, know your exits, and never sleep in the open.
It's so dark. The ground drinks the light.
I think the dunes are watching us. I know they can't.
Please don't let me be left behind in the black.
This whole country looks like the end of a very long book.
Where does the sky end and the sand begin? I can't tell.
I know this sand. It's the sand where my kind gather to forget.
The city ahead is full of us. Not all of us are well.
The old empire is a rumour here. It's also a wound.
The dunes hum. It might be machinery. It might be memory.
The city in the dunes is the last of us. I am not sure I want to meet them.
Dragging a prisoner across the ash. The ash will eat the evidence. And us, if we linger.
We could drop the dead weight and let the ash take him. I'm only saying it aloud.
The prisoner is silent. That's a mercy. The ash doesn't like noise.
Someone will want him badly in these domes. We shouldn't be the ones to find out who.
Every domed lord could use a new captive.
He weighs more every step. The ash is in his clothes. We should have left him at the road.
He won't wake until we're out of the ash. Good. I hate arguing with sleepers.
Keep him quiet, keep him covered. The Legion does not care who it takes.
He's dead weight in all the senses. I carry him anyway.
I once carried a man farther than this. He didn't thank me either.
Please don't hand him to the domes. I've heard what lives in the second one.
I don't want to hear about the domes any more. I want to leave. With him.
He's breathing. I keep checking that he's breathing.
Every shadow looks like it wants him. Why do the shadows want him?
We don't belong here. Neither does he. Let us go.
A captive in the ash. Even the Legion would find this tasteless.
Cargo secure. Environment poor. Likelihood of seizure by hostile units: high.
The captive is awake. He has stopped speaking. I'll take that as acceptance.
I've been taken before. It doesn't make this easier.
The plain remembers prisoners. It's reminded each time one crosses it.
My legs are going. The ash is thick. If I fall, drag me out, do not argue.
I'm fading. The ash is in my chest. If I stop, drag me, don't wait.
Pain I can do. Weakness I can do. The ash I can't.
I didn't expect to fall here. Funny.
Do not spend a bandage on me yet. Spend the time.
I'm hurt. I'm telling you now so nobody is surprised in the middle of the plain.
I'll make it to the edge, if the edge is near. If it isn't, tell me.
A cut like this is nothing, anywhere else. Here the ash gets into it.
Tell me if I begin to lag. I won't tell you.
Keep the line tight and keep your eyes up. I'll keep up.
Please. I'm not well. Please don't leave me in the ash.
I can't feel my fingers. Is that normal? Is that normal here?
It hurts when I breathe. It hurts when I don't.
I'm so cold. Why is it so cold if it's ash?
Don't leave me. Don't leave me.
Body failing. Ash entering the joints.
Structural damage is considerable. Motion is possible but poor.
Grit is entering the joint housing.
I'd prefer to end in the open air, not in a dome.
Primary systems failing. This location isn't recommended for failing.
Do you know what it's to be forgiven by everyone but yourself? It's a very orderly kind of misery.
They told me it was weather. They told me it was fate. I preferred my own account: it was me.
I wrote my resignation a hundred times. There was no one to hand it to. I keep them in the drawer.
I couldn't have foreseen it. I know. And still the blame fits me like a coat tailored in the dark.
If you find a way to fix a famine, tell me. I will keep the form open for you.
Is there anything you want done? Anything? I don't mind what it is. I only like to be asked.
I'd carry your bags. I'd carry your enemies. I'd carry them very carefully.
Some people told me not to help certain people. I did not understand which. Everybody needs help.
The best part of my day is when someone gives me a task. The second best is finishing it.
You haven't asked for anything yet. That's all right. I'll wait. I'm very good at waiting.
The exile is ended. The Legion has no more to keep. The Legion walks on out of habit.
The emperor is dead. We are told this by those who killed him.
Our warden duty is done. The Legion doesn't know what comes after warden duty.
We weren't his friends. We weren't his enemies.
There's no emperor to guard. We stand in the doorway. We have nowhere to go.
You ended the emperor. We could not. We hold that against you. We hold that against ourselves.
The exile was a mercy. You took the mercy. The Legion will take your parts.
We were the door and you went through it. Now we go through you.
The emperor is dead. The door is open. We remain standing in it.
Now the Legion has no cause. We have you.
We sought release for ten centuries. You gave it to him, not to us.
You've come from the other domes. I can tell. You smell of the same silence.
Someone has been in the domes. The thralls are agitated. Will you tell me what happened?
I felt the second dome go quiet. The thralls feel it too. Was it you? Please sit.
The second dome used to hum. It has stopped. I was sorry to hear it stop.
Something has changed in the domes. I can feel it in the grain. Will you sit?

states: Head of Agriculture killed by player

say: I haven't heard from the first dome in a while. Is the Head of Agriculture busy? I could help him.
The signals have gone quiet. Perhaps everyone has finally decided to rest.
Is the first dome all right? I sent a message. He hasn't replied.
I have not heard that sad voice from the first dome in a while. I hope he is not unwell.
I made soup for the Head of Agriculture. He always liked soup. Have you seen him?
Tech hunters find the best loot in the ash and bring back the worst dreams.
I took a core off a cleanser, once. Nobody warned me it screamed when it died.
We have a code for the domes. Don't look in them, don't touch the doors, don't sleep near them.
The rule for the domes is simple: don't knock. The rule for the ash is simpler: don't stop.
I met a hunter once who went in for a power cell. He came out as a different species of man.
Never sell the cores to a skeleton who asks too many questions. They can tell what they are.
Every tech hunter is half scavenger, half gravedigger. The ash has more graves than loot.
I saw a thrall reading a book once. Upside-down. It didn't turn it over.
The empire kept better records than anyone alive. Pity the records are all on slates no one can read.
I heard a thrall humming once. Not a tune, exactly.
If you want to survive the domes, forget your name. They collect names.
The best finds come from the quietest places. The quietest places have reasons.
Skeletons built the domes. Skeletons also filled the prisons. I'm one of them, and I know it.
The Legion is what happens to skeletons who side with the wrong lord. I keep my head and my opinions to myself.
I met a no-head once. It stood by my chair all evening. I think it wanted a drink.
They say the Head of Agriculture still counts grain that isn't there. That's the sort of guilt I fear.
Some of us remember the old days. Most of us pretend we don't. It's easier that way.
The elders say the Holy Nation was a small faith once, and the old empire sat on it. It didn't die of it.
Skeletons ruled the old empire and the empire starved. The Holy Nation remembers what machines do to the faithful.
They say the first believers were hunted by the empire police. I do not wish to know more.
The Holy Nation didn't rise from nothing. It rose from the shadow of an empire that tried to bury it.
The empire put its boot on our first believers. We remember the boot.
The Empire's wolves hunted our first believers through the dark years.
Every UC town carries the old empire in its bones. The laws, the cats, the stamps. We forgot the hunger, but not the forms.
I heard the Second Empire kept child prisons. Funny how our magistrates sometimes sound the same.
The dead empire's last emperor is a mad skeleton in a dome, and we still spend his name every day.
We keep the stamps, the cats, the records. We lost the reason, but never the paperwork.
The Second Empire is gone and left behind a flag and a forest of regulations.
The old Emperor's laws are still on our books. Only the prisons have changed names.
